content:
• #1

A diversion of inbound aircraft to holding patterns began today at Charles de Gaulle airport (CDG) between ~18:49-18:50 UTC (local time is UTC+1). AFR54ZW and AFR31BE diverted just before lining up for the final approach on parallel runways, at approximately the same time. Several incoming flights on final approach ahead of those two were allowed to continue and land but those farther away (starting with AFR54ZW and AFR31BE) were diverted to holding patterns upstream of the approach path.

It continued for about 17 minutes until about 19:06:45 UTC when AFR54ZW and AFR31BE left their holding patterns and proceeded towards the airport to land, followed by the others.

Flights continued to depart to the west during this timeframe so it seems that only the approach side (east) was affected. But there were flights which departed by taking off to the west which then had to fly east and looped around and flew over the holding patterns. For example LOT2EB and THY6432 pictured below. So the concern which caused the stop must have been isolated to pretty low altitudes on the eastern side of the airport.

Once the airspace was deemed safe, inbound aircraft were cleared to resume their approaches to both the North and South runways. Normal flight operations officially resumed at 20:15 local time.

Airport officials have not yet released further details regarding the nature of the sighting or whether local law enforcement has launched an investigation into the incident.
